approachQuestion.prompt:
Best Sum from k Consecutive Days

The array `changes` gives the change in a score on each consecutive day. Values may be positive, zero, or negative. Return the greatest sum among segments of exactly `k` consecutive days. You may not skip days or change the input. Return the sum even when every allowed sum is negative.

Limits and assumptions:
• 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ k ≤ n; −10^9 ≤ changes[i] ≤ 10^9.
• Every sum fits in a 64-bit integer.
• Every candidate segment has exactly k values; values may have any sign.

Examples:
1. changes = [4,-8,6,2,-1,5], k = 3 → 7, for [6,2,-1].
2. changes = [-5,-2,-9], k = 2 → -7, for [-5,-2].

Choose one approach.
constraints: Every sum fits in a 64-bit integer.
Every candidate segment has exactly k values; values may have any sign.

options.text: Sum the first k days. Then move the window one day at a time: subtract the value that leaves and add the new value. Keep the greatest sum seen.
options.feedback: Every segment has the same length, so each new sum comes from the previous one by replacing one value. This remains true for negative values.

options.text: Calculate the sum of every length-k segment, store all sums in an array, then find the greatest.
options.feedback: Every sum is calculated correctly, but the full list is unnecessary when the output is a single maximum.

options.text: Sort all changes in descending order and add the k largest values.
options.feedback: The days must be consecutive. For [100,1,100] with k = 2, this returns 200, while each allowed pair sums to 101.

options.text: Move the length-k window and stop when its new sum is lower than the previous window sum.
options.feedback: Window sums can fall and then rise. For [5,5,-100,100,100] with k = 2, the sums are 10, -95, 0, 200; stopping at the first drop misses the maximum of 200.

feedback.reason: Check whether the window property and the boundary movements match the exact task conditions.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the method “Move a fixed-length k window by subtracting the outgoing value and adding the incoming value,” choose one pair: running time and additional space.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Do not count the input or returned value as additional space.
There is no recursion or call stack.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) additional space

feedback.reason: The first window takes k additions. Each later window takes one subtraction and one addition. Only the current sum and best sum are kept.

details.correctness: Every candidate has length k. Moving the start one position removes exactly changes[left] and adds exactly changes[right]. This update also works for negative values. Initializing the first window and processing all later windows together touch the array only a constant number of times per position.
details.alternatives: Storing every sum is correct but unnecessary when only the maximum is returned. Sorting breaks the adjacency requirement. Stopping after a drop is wrong because later windows may have a greater sum. Negative values do not justify stopping early or returning an empty result when exactly k days are required.

methodReveal.title: A fixed-length window sum
methodReveal.description: Sum the first k changes. For each move, subtract the value leaving on the left, add the value entering on the right, and update the greatest sum.
